newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOCOM precious metals end firmer on yen's retreat.
newsitem.headline: TOCOM precious metals end firmer on yen's retreat.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo precious metals futures ended mostly firmer on Friday, with sentiment supported by the yen's retreat against the dollar, traders said.
Benchmark April gold was up six yen at 1,301 yen per gram.
The May contract fell four yen while other months ranged from six to eight yen higher.

Investors were both sellers and buyers of gold futures, traders said. "Some private investors were liquidating their longs, while some investors hunted for bargains. But concern over the possibility that the yen will rise again, limited gains," one trader said.
Spot gold was quoted at $347.20/50 per ounce at 0728 GMT, against $347.20/70 in New York on Thursday.
News on Thursday that Germany's Bundesbank not sell gold but revalue its reserves had little impact on the bullion market, traders said. They said currency rates would be the key to market direction.

Platinum futures ended mostly higher in line with gold, while palladium futures settled firmer after drifting within a tight range. "Market participants are watching over when Russian exports of platinum group metals (PGM) to Japan will resume," an analyst at a commodity broker said.

"The Russian platinum group metal agency (Almaz) has asked Japanese clients how much volume of PGM Japan want for 1997. We have answered by fax and are waiting for a reply from Almaz," an official at a bullion house said.

Traders expect Russian PGM shipments to resume in June or July, but they said supply tightness in the palladium market due to Russia's suspension of PGM exports for the last five months, would not be immediately resolved.
Benchmark April platinum was up six yen at 1,431 yen. Benchmark April palladium was up two yen at 600 yen. Benchmark April silver was up 1.3 yen per 10 grams at 184.5 yen.
